| **Best grocery/meal-kit hybrid** | **Hungryroot** | Best if you want ultra-fast “assemble and cook” meals plus groceries/snacks in one order. It’s more flexible than a traditional meal kit and can work well for mixed diets. Hungryroot lists dinners “as low as $8.99 per serving.” ([sprout.hungryroot.com](https://sprout.hungryroot.com/questions/?utm_source=openai)) | Can stay near budget, but pricing depends heavily on cart size and credits; best if you’ll use the grocery items too. |
| **Best if variety matters more than strict budget** | **HelloFresh** | Very strong mixed-household option: large weekly menu, vegetarian plan, and meals marketed as ~30 minutes; you can choose 2–6 vegetarian recipes per week for two or four people. ([hellofresh.com](https://www.hellofresh.com/eat/vegetarian-meal-delivery)) | Slightly above your target after shipping: 2 people × 3 dinners is currently about **$87.93/week all-in**, or **~$14.66/serving**. ([mealfan.com](https://www.mealfan.com/meal-delivery-price-index/)) |

## My recommendation

**Start with Dinnerly or EveryPlate.**  
- Choose **EveryPlate** if **price is the priority** and you’re okay with simpler meals and fewer vegetarian choices.  
- Choose **Dinnerly** if you want to stay around **$12/serving all-in** while getting more variety and a better chance that both of you find meals you like.

If you’re willing to go a little over budget for convenience and selection, **HelloFresh** is probably the easiest “mixed couple” pick—but I’d wait for a promo or use it selectively because the all-in cost can exceed your target.  

I’d **skip Green Chef and Purple Carrot for now** unless organic or fully plant-based meals are more important than budget: Green Chef is around **$15.16/serving all-in** for 2 people × 3 dinners, and Purple Carrot’s vegan meal kits run about **$13.25–$14.25/serving before some shipping scenarios**. ([mealfan.com](https://www.mealfan.com/meal-delivery-price-index/))
